say: This guy thinks he's beaten the speed cameras. Slam the brakes at the camera, then floor it. Let's *see.*
Motorway. The gantries say *fifty,* in a red ring. And the signs say *average* speed check. Gary sets his cruise control at fifty.
Behind him, Kev. Brand new sports car. Doing *seventy,* and in a hurry.
Kev flies past, cuts in front of Gary. Then he sees the camera, and *slams* on the brakes.
Gary's left a *two* *second* gap, so he slows down in time.
Kev crawls past the camera at fifty. *No* *flash.* He's laughing.
Then he floors it again. *Seventy.* Until the next camera. *Brakes.*
He even changes lanes, because everyone knows they can't catch you if you switch lanes. *Right?*
Two weeks later, a letter lands on Kev's *doormat.*
Rule two six one. A speed limit in a *red* *ring* on a motorway is the legal limit. You must not go over it.
These are *average* speed cameras. They time you from one camera to the next. Braking at the camera doesn't change your *average.*
They watch *every* *lane.* And they don't flash. No flash doesn't mean you got away with it.
Kev averaged sixty eight in a fifty. That's not just a hundred pound fine. That can mean *court.* Four to six points, or a *ban.*
And slamming on the brakes for no reason can be *careless* *driving* too.
Kev, *guilty.* Would you have braked at the camera? Follow for case five.
